interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include a negative surgical margin (0.0), no seminal vesicle invasion (0.0), absence of lymphovascular invasion (0.0), and no lymph node metastasis (0.0). The preoperative PSA was elevated at 19. The surgical pathology showed a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT2c, with no extraprostatic extension. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA level and the pathological grade of the cancer. The biopsy findings showed a discrepancy, with one session indicating ISUP grade group 2 and the other ISUP grade group 3. Nodal status was documented as negative.

Information that would revise this prognosis significantly includes the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory. A documented postoperative PSA level and its trend would be crucial in assessing recurrence risk. The current uncertainty in the prognosis is partly due to the absence of previous notes, which limits the assessment of the patient's prior status and postoperative course. The fixed estimated horizon is 62.29 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 46.72–77.86 months; its coverage has not been validated.
